counterfactual_missing_items: Lyme serology, autoimmune panel, comprehensive paraneoplastic antibody panel, and CSF cytology were negative
No pain, hematuria, fever, visual changes, or speech/swallowing difficulty was present
Plantar responses were flexor, not upper motor neuron, reducing CNS/myelopathic causes
decisive_items: bilateral femoral nerve enlargement without enhancement
bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
response.rationale: R1 captures the primary diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy by combining the progressive lower-extremity weakness, lumbosacral-predominant motor picture, and bilateral femoral nerve enlargement. C1 is the same fundamental diagnosis with the anatomical MRI finding appended, so it is only a correlated/non-independent runner-up and not the best identity. R3 is less likely because CIDP would not directly explain the chronic lumbosacral plexopathy, bladder involvement, 100-lb weight loss, or femoral nerve enlargement as the dominant clinical tie to the diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus process.

rejected.why: CIDP can parallel the demyelinating EDX and elevated CSF protein, but it does not explain the superimposed chronic lumbosacral plexopathy, bilateral femoral nerve enlargement, urinary retention, and severe paraneoplastic-like weight loss as unified by diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy.
